detail.longDescription: arXiv:2603.14449v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Aligning speech agents' response initiation with users' expectations remains challenging. We introduce Tap-to-Adapt, a framework for interactive speech systems in which manual activation and interruption provide both immediate response control and online supervision for personalized initiation timing. To learn from sparse corrections and recent feedback, we introduce \emph{Balanced Proximal Replay for History-conditioned Timing} (BPRHT) as its response initiation timing control mechanism, combining frozen speech representations, class-balanced replay with proximal regularization, and recent correction history. We evaluate acoustic backbones for BPRHT on recorded speech and compare update rules and recent-history configurations in simulation. The selected replay and history mechanisms lower simulated correction rates relative to their respective baselines. To reduce new users' cold-start correction burden, we evaluate shared initialization in a two-stage user study. Stage~1 established shared initialization with 20 participants, locking the average of earlier participants' final heads upon parameter and opening-correction plateaus. Stage~2 assigned 48 new participants equally to online adaptation with or without shared initialization, or frozen shared initialization. Online adaptation without shared initialization had more opening corrections per minute than with it (rate ratio 1.69, 95\% confidence interval 1.15--2.49). Final-block correction rates were similar across conditions. Online updates accompanied reported speaking and waiting adjustments. Declining corrections under frozen parameters also suggest user accommodation. Code and 1,000 labeled pilot recordings are available at: https://github.com/ZihongHe/tap_to_adapt
